'''Alexander Valentinovich Zakharov''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Алекса́ндр Валенти́нович Заха́ров}}, born June 1, 1941) is a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] and Russian chief scientist and astronomer serving at the [[Russian Space Research Institute]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/tech/science/space/story/2012-01-08/russian-mars-probe/52457434/1|title=Underfunding doomed Russian Mars probe, lawyer says|last=Vergano|first=Dan|date=2012-01-08|work=[[USA Today]]|quote=mission scientist Alexander Zakharov of the Space Research Institute in Moscow|access-date=23 March 2012}}</ref> (IKI).

He was a lead scientist of the failed Mars missions, [[Mars 96]] and [[Fobos-Grunt]].<ref name="Reuters">{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/russia-spacecraft-idUSL5E8CV3TU20120131|title=Russia blames Mars probe failure on space radiation|last=de Carbonnel|first=Alissa|date=2012-01-31|publisher=[[Reuters]]|access-date=27 February 2012}}</ref><ref name="mt_prelaunch">{{cite news|url=http://www.themoscowtimes.com/news/article/mars-moon-lander-to-return-russia-to-deep-space/447350.html|title=Mars Moon Lander to Return Russia to Deep Space |publisher=The Moscow Times|date=8 Nov 2011}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Three days after the end of ''Mars 96'', Zakharov came up to the conclusion that there was a flaw in the spacecraft control system, and proposed another attempt for another Mars mission.<ref>{{cite news|title=Life After Mars '96 |url=http://news.sciencemag.org/sciencenow/1996/11/20-04.html |newspaper=Science NOW |date=20 November 1996 |access-date=23 March 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130621012023/http://news.sciencemag.org/sciencenow/1996/11/20-04.html |archive-date=21 June 2013 }}</ref>

In 1999, he became a project scientist on the feasibility of the [[Fobos-Grunt]] sample return mission.<ref name="mt_prelaunch"/>

In November 2007, he was interviewed by [[Mat Kaplan]] on ''Planetary Radio'' along with Bruce Betts and Tom Duxbury.<ref>{{Cite episode |title="To Phobos and Back" |url=http://www.planetary.org/radio/show/00000262/ |series="Planetary Radio" |date=November 13, 2007 |number=262 |minutes=00:25:52 |access-date=April 13, 2012 |archive-date=November 22, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081122032540/http://www.planetary.org/radio/show/00000262/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2008, he became a member of [[The Planetary Society]]'s [[Living Interplanetary Flight Experiment]] team. He was responsible for placing the LIFE biomodule into the return capsule.

He forwarded the letter about the Fobos-Grunt failure to the Planetary Society members.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://planetary.org/blogs/emily-lakdawalla/2011/3298.html|title=Phobos-Grunt: All but over, a letter from IKI}}</ref> After the probe's fall into the southern [[Pacific Ocean]] on January 15, 2012, he commented that this crash was a tragedy for the Russian scientific community, and that with soil samples from Phobos his team could uncover information about the solar system's origins.<ref>{{cite news |title=Phobos-Grunt Crashes Into the Pacific |first=Katharine |last=Sanderson |url=http://www.astrobio.net/pressrelease/4476/phobos-grunt-crashes-into-the-pacific |newspaper=Astrobiology Magazine |date=January 18, 2012 |access-date=28 March 2012}}</ref> Later, he told [[Reuters]] about the possible reasons of the probe stranded in low Earth orbit, but doesn't rule out something. He then suggested there was some kind of problem with the flight system or the programming, which were not designed to guard against the space radiation.<ref name="Reuters"/>

He was hoping that Fobos-Grunt will be repeated as called by IKI's director [[Lev Zeleny]] and later acknowledged by Roscosmos in April 2012. However, with an agreement for cooperation with the [[European Space Agency]] on [[ExoMars]] had been reached, the space agency chose to focus on that program instead, but not ruled out any possible future Phobos sample return mission.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.space.com/13870-russia-phobos-grunt-spacecraft-life.html|title=Scientist: Russia's Failed Mars' Moon Probe Worth a Second Try|last=Warmflash|first=David|website=[[Space.com]] |date=2011-12-08|access-date=11 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Russia's participation in the "ExoMars" does not cancel the plans for the "Phobos-Grunt-2" |url=http://www.ria.ru/science/20120320/600999665.html |newspaper=[[RIA Novosti]] |date=20 March 2012 |access-date=3 April 2012}}</ref>

Zakharov will be attending the Asia Oceania Geosciences Society AGU (WPGM) Joint Assembly from 13 to 17 August 2012 at [[Resorts World Sentosa]], [[Singapore]] for the presentation on Mars Science and Exploration.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asiaoceania.org/aogs2012/public.asp?page=mars2/confSessionList.asp |title=AOGS - AGU (WPGM) Joint Assembly 2012 |access-date=12 April 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120511103721/http://www.asiaoceania.org/aogs2012/public.asp?page=mars2%2FconfSessionList.asp |archive-date=11 May 2012 }}</ref>{{clarify|date=April 2012|reason=ideally needs reword or more coverage than just a conference schedule, why not wait until after the conference to avoid future looking claims?}}
